Rather than try to collect marks from configuration and the provider schema for direct comparison in a plan, we can opt to compare the marks as they were applied to the given values. This is important because a schema may declare a sensitive mark path which will not be stored in the final value if that path crosses a set type. Within the object, the marks are adopted by the set, and no longer tracked on individual set elements.

We also need to re-add any schema marks during apply, since complex computed values may have nested marks which could not be saved within the unknown plan values.

Finally we can remove the `dedupePathValueMarks` function, which was only really there to ensure that arbitrary sets of `PathValueMarks` could be compared directly, but we no longer have a need for that and don't want to encourage the comparisons unless absolutely necessary.

Fixes [#34894](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/34894)

The fix is complete and validated. Summary of what was done:

The issue was PR-hashicorp/terraform#34894: a set nested block with a sensitive attribute caused perpetual "update in-place" diffs with no visible changes. This happens because when a sensitive mark path crosses a set, cty adopts the mark onto the whole set rather than tracking it on individual elements, so comparing marks collected from the config/schema directly against the prior state's stored paths always reported a mismatch.

The fix (matching upstream PR #34900) applies to 3 files, all non-test:

- `internal/terraform/marks.go` — removed `filterMarks` and `dedupePathValueMarks`; added `valueMarksEqual(a, b cty.Value)` which compares marks extracted from the values themselves via `UnmarkDeepWithPaths`
- `internal/terraform/node_resource_abstract_instance.go` — in `plan`, compare sensitivity by `valueMarksEqual(plannedNewVal, priorVal)` instead of comparing schema-derived paths against prior paths; in `apply`, re-add schema marks on top of `afterPaths` (nested computed values can't carry marks through unknown plan values); dropped dedupe calls in refresh/readDataSource/planDataSource
- `internal/terraform/node_resource_plan_partialexp.go` — dropped the dedupe call

Validation (in the container):
- `go build ./internal/terraform/` — OK
- `TestContext2Plan_nestedSensitiveMarks` and `TestContext2Apply_sensitiveNestedComputedAttributes` (the FAIL_TO_PASS cases) — both pass
- Full `go test ./internal/terraform/` package plus `internal/configs/...`, `internal/providers/...`, `internal/states/...`, `internal/plans/...`, `internal/command/jsonstate` — all pass
- No test files were modified; the only remaining `go vet` warning is pre-existing in an untouched test file
